headline: 雷利史考特新片遇冷
context: 雷利·史考特（Ridley Scott）耗資 1.1 億美元改編小說《The Dog Stars》，卻被影評批評步調拖沓、缺乏新意。愛丁堡藝穗節上，喜劇演員麥斯·奧勒斯克帶來個人秀，講述他為了與伴侶結婚，從自由派猶太教轉向正統派的心路歷程。英國樂團 Adam and the Ants 的吉他手，也回顧了樂團 1980 年一夕爆紅的瘋狂歲月。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: An adaptation of Peter Heller’s 2012 novel never finds its footing with overly familiar survival beats and a glum lack of energy Looking towards the end of an August movie dumping ground littered with more unwanted trash than usual, there seemed to be a faint glimmer of hope, a shiny treasure poking out through the dusty mass of unnecessary sequels and sex purge romcoms . Somehow, there was a $110m-budget adaptation of an acclaimed novel directed by Ridley Scott, led by a recently Oscar-nominated rising star with support from two Oscar-nominated actors and an Oscar winner. But why then would such a film be unveiled in between the summer blockbuster season and the upcoming deluge of prestige fall festival big hitters? A cursed weekend that’s recently been home to Jay Roach’s heinous War of the Roses remake, Dennis Quaid’s Ronald Reagan biopic and George Miller’s hard-to-define and even harder-to-love flop Three Thousand Years of Longing. Ever since The Dog Stars, based on Peter Heller’s 2012 novel, had been yanked from its far more encouraging date at the end of March, there were multiple red flags flying and the rotten end of August has ultimately become an appropriate punishment for a limp and lethargic film that only briefly fascinates in pushing us to wonder what anyone was really hoping this would end up being. It’s yet another grubby postapocalyptic survival tale, an overcrowded subgenre that hasn’t just reached maximum capacity on the big screen but on the small one too. In a world of seven Walking Dead shows, the beats are now far too familiar – artfully dishevelled actors grieve for the past and fear for the future as they scramble to find and protect resources – and there’s nothing new or notable here to conjure anything but deja vu. sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: With their twangy sound, madcap outfits, lusty yodelling and pirouetting pirate frontman, the band became global superstars almost overnight. But, as their guitarist Marco Pirroni recalls, the thrill ride soon hit the buffers ‘The essence of pop is, one, brilliant fucking songs – and the rest is sex, subversion, style and humour. And that was us .” So Adam Ant told me in 1995, describing the reconstructed Adam and the Ants, which formed in early 1980 with the arrival of guitarist/songwriter Marco Pirroni, who was sitting next to him. “We’re responsible for bringing back dressing up, going mad and screaming your head off.” “That’s it!” grins Pirroni when I remind him of this, as we sit in the shabby-chic lounge of London’s 21Soho venue. Back then, I didn’t tell them I was 15 in 1980, forever sprinting across dancefloors pretending to be Adam Ant, chiffon scarves tied to knees, limbs flailing like a whirling Cossack. Pirroni hears this today and laughs. “That’s what it’s all about,” he hoots. “When I was 13, watching Bowie, Roxy, T Rex, you just go, ‘I wanna do that.’ It’s exciting, sexy, about looking good, Top of the Pops. I can’t imagine anyone saying, ‘Wow, I desperately want to be in Cabaret Voltaire. They must be earning no money, look boring and nobody likes them – that’s the band for me!’” Continue reading...

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Pleasance Dome, Edinburgh This show about Olesker’s lengthy journey to becoming an Orthodox Jew in order to marry his partner is both elegant and nuanced ‘I would do anything for love,” Meat Loaf sang, “but I won’t do that.” Max Olesker would, if his solo show Making the Cut – based on his memoir – is any guide. It recounts the comic and writer’s conversion from liberal to Orthodox Judaism, a process required so he can marry his sweetheart – but which, in the meantime, forbids him from so much as touching her for years on end, and forbids much else besides. Secularists may be left reeling. Olesker himself clearly has deeply ambivalent feelings about what he’s gone through. That all makes for a gripping story, of course, that begins when this former half of Max and Ivan meets his dream woman at the Edinburgh fringe. He’s Jewish, she’s Jewish: what’s the problem? It’s that the Olesker family’s loose-fitting and bohemian religious tradition is not considered Jewish by his fiancee’s. If love’s young dream is to be fulfilled, Max must renounce his name, foreswear his profession, keep his hands off his fiancee, visit synagogue three times a day in seeming perpetuity – oh, and get circumcised, too. (Who said romance was dead?) Continue reading...

thread_text: 衛報影評砲轟雷利·史考特斥資 1.1 億美元改編的新片《The Dog Stars》，直指步調拖沓、老套，是這個檔期的失手之作。愛丁堡藝穗節上，喜劇演員麥斯·奧勒斯克帶來個人秀，講述他為了與伴侶結婚，從自由派猶太教轉向正統派的心路歷程。Adam and the Ants 的吉他手馬可·皮羅尼，也回顧了樂團 1980 年一夕爆紅的瘋狂歲月。
threads_text: 衛報影評砲轟雷利·史考特斥資 1.1 億美元改編的小說電影《The Dog Stars》，批評步調拖沓、劇情老套，形容是這個檔期的失手之作。愛丁堡藝穗節上，喜劇演員麥斯·奧勒斯克帶來一齣個人秀，講述他為了與伴侶結婚，從自由派猶太教轉向正統派、期間得暫時不能碰觸伴侶的漫長過程。英國樂團 Adam and the Ants 的吉他手馬可·皮羅尼，則在專訪中回顧了樂團 1980 年一夕爆紅、又迅速降溫的瘋狂歲月。
voice_text: 雷利·史考特的新片評價不太好。這部《The Dog Stars》改編自小說，砸了一億一千萬美元，卻被說步調拖沓、老套，是這個檔期的失手之作。愛丁堡藝穗節上，喜劇演員麥斯·奧勒斯克帶來一齣個人秀，講他為了跟伴侶結婚，從自由派猶太教轉向正統派的過程。英國樂團 Adam and the Ants 的吉他手，也回顧了樂團一九八零年一夕爆紅的瘋狂歲月。
